metadata.title: GEEK Protocol — KasWare application integration
metadata.schema: correctIndex is zero-based; options contains four distinct strings
metadata.reviewNotice: Internally source-checked original questions scoped to this KasWare browser-extension revision. Not universal wallet behavior, an installed-version claim, a security audit or an endorsement. Difficulty is provisional.
metadata.attribution: GEEK Protocol original questions based on pinned primary implementation evidence; no source code or prose imported.

questions.prompt: Where does the cited KasWare extension expose its browser wallet API?
options: window.kasware
window.kaspad
document.walletSecret
navigator.krc20
questions.funFact: The injected provider is exposed through window.kasware; it is the application interface, not a private-key export.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: Which browser event does the cited KasWare code dispatch after exposing its injected provider?
options: accountsChanged
kasware#initialized
networkChanged
virtual-chain-changed
questions.funFact: The injection announcement is kasware#initialized. Account, network and node-chain events have different purposes.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: Which cited KasWare method reads available authorized accounts and returns an empty list for an unauthorized site?
options: requestAccounts()
getPublicKey()
getAccounts()
getNetwork()
questions.funFact: getAccounts checks the calling origin and returns [] without connection permission; requestAccounts uses the connection approval flow.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: For an ordinary external site, what does the cited KasWare permission service use to look up connection authorization?
options: The requested token ticker
The recipient's address prefix
The transaction fee amount
The site's origin
questions.funFact: External connection records are keyed by origin, and hasPermission also requires the stored site to be connected.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: In the cited KasWare request flow, does an existing site connection by itself skip a required signing approval?
options: No; the operation approval check runs after the connection check
Yes; connection permanently approves all later signatures
Yes; every connected site becomes a SAFE method
Only if the site requests an unrecognized method
questions.funFact: The connection check and operation-specific APPROVAL metadata are separate stages. A connection is not blanket signing consent.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: What does the cited KasWare flow request when a non-SAFE operation reaches a locked keyring?
options: An automatic wallet reset
An unlock approval before continuing
A fresh seed phrase from the website
A transaction broadcast without a signature
questions.funFact: The non-SAFE request path checks isUnlocked and waits for the wallet unlock approval before moving on.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: What unit should an application use for the payment amount passed to the cited KasWare sendKaspa method?
options: Whole KAS entered as a decimal string
The number of recipient UTXOs
Sompi
A percentage of the wallet balance
questions.funFact: The interface names and forwards its amount argument as sompi. Applications must match that unit when constructing a payment request.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: Which cited KasWare provider method requests KRC-20 holdings rather than the native KAS balance summary?
options: getBalance()
getPublicKey()
getUtxoEntries()
getKRC20Balance()
questions.funFact: The controller reads address inscriptions for getKRC20Balance; getBalance returns the native confirmed, unconfirmed and total amounts.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: When the cited KasWare accountsChanged handler detects a changed active account, what does it emit to the application?
options: The updated account-address array
Only a transaction ID
The mnemonic for the new account
Only the network name
questions.funFact: The handler updates its selected address and account list, then emits accountsChanged with the accounts array.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: Which provider event carries a changed network name in the cited KasWare implementation?
options: accountsChanged
networkChanged
maturity
virtual-chain-changed
questions.funFact: The handler compares the new network with its cached network and emits networkChanged with the changed name.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: How does the cited KasWare disconnect handler change its cached account state?
options: It retains both as currently authorized
It replaces the address with a new seed phrase
It clears the account list and selected address
It changes the selected account into a mainnet account
questions.funFact: Disconnection clears the cached accounts and selected address, marks the provider disconnected and emits an empty accountsChanged list.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: Which cited KasWare method returns the wallet software VERSION value for compatibility checks?
options: getNetwork()
getPublicKey()
getBalance()
getVersion()
questions.funFact: getVersion returns the extension VERSION constant. Network and account queries describe different aspects of the wallet session.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: What does a caller supply to the cited KasWare pushTx method?
options: A raw transaction string to submit
A mnemonic to import
A human-readable message to sign
A list of account names to activate
questions.funFact: pushTx forwards rawtx for transaction submission. Its input is not a seed phrase or a message-signing request.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: What happens when an application calls signKRC20BatchTransferTransaction in the cited KasWare page provider?
options: It silently executes a native KAS payment
It throws a deprecation error naming krc20BatchTransferTransaction
It returns the current KRC-20 balance
It switches to mainnet and retries
questions.funFact: The deprecated page-provider method throws before submitting a request, directing callers to krc20BatchTransferTransaction.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: In the cited KasWare signPskt options, what does each signInputs entry specify?
options: An output address and a token ticker
An account nickname and a password hint
An input index and its sighashType
A block hash and a confirmation count
questions.funFact: Each entry pairs index with sighashType so the request can describe input-specific signing intent. The schema alone is not proof of a wallet execution result.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: Why should an integrator examine numeric precision in the cited KasWare getUtxoEntries serialization?
options: It encodes all integers as exact decimal strings
It encrypts every amount with a public address
It omits every value above one sompi
It converts bigint values to Number, which can lose integer precision above the safe range
questions.funFact: The JSON replacer explicitly converts bigint to Number. JavaScript Numbers do not preserve all integers above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; this is a conversion caveat, not a claim that an observed balance was wrong.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: For an authorized caller with a current account, how does the cited KasWare getUtxoEntries choose the queried address?
options: It uses the supplied address when truthy, otherwise the current account address
It always queries every account in the wallet
It uses only the recipient of the last transaction
It always substitutes the mainnet genesis address
questions.funFact: The controller sends either [address] or [account.address] to the UTXO service. Permission and current-account checks run first.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: Which three values does the cited KasWare verifyMessage interface accept?
options: A private key, mnemonic and password
A public key, message and signature
A block hash, nonce and difficulty target
A token ticker, mint limit and maximum supply
questions.funFact: verifyMessage forwards pubkey, message and sig for verification; it does not ask the application to provide signing secrets.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: How does the cited KasWare RPC flow handle a method with no corresponding provider-controller handler?
options: It falls back to sendKaspa
It treats the method name as a message to sign
It throws a methodNotFound RPC error
It creates a connected-site record and reports success
questions.funFact: The first flow stage resolves the method name and rejects missing handlers before later approval and execution stages.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.

questions.prompt: If a background request rejects, what does the cited KasWare page provider do with the error?
options: It replaces the error with a successful transaction ID
It hides the rejection and returns an empty signature
It automatically retries the request as a payment
It serializes and rethrows the error to the caller
questions.funFact: The _request catch handler rethrows serializeError(err), so the application must handle the rejected promise rather than assume success.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited KasWare implementation; source code and prose are not imported.
